summary.tagline: Discover one of Scotland's most remote and beautiful beaches, guarded by the sea-stack Am Buachaille.
summary.seo_title: Visiting Sandwood Bay | Remote Scottish Coastline

travel.headline: Responsible Access in a Crofting Estate
travel.reservation: No formal entry permit is required to visit the bay, which is managed by the John Muir Trust. Visitors must respect that Sandwood is an active crofting estate; check for local guidance on livestock and land management before setting out.

days.title: Trek to the Remote Coast

stops.name: Sandwood Bay
stops.detail: Hike the four-mile path across exposed moorland to reach this expansive beach, characterized by its size and the iconic sea-stack Am Buachaille.

days.driving: Allow time for the 8-mile round-trip walk; conditions vary significantly based on weather.
days.note: The path across the moorland can be uneven and wet; appropriate footwear and clothing are essential for the exposed environment.

intel.title: Moorland Path
intel.text: The route from Blairmore involves crossing four miles of exposed moorland that is often wet underfoot. Ensure you are prepared for changing weather conditions as there is little shelter.

intel.title: Daylight Considerations
intel.text: Allow significant time for the return journey to Blairmore to ensure you are off the moorland before dark. The terrain requires a steady pace that may be slower than typical walking speeds.

intel.title: Blairmore Departure
intel.text: The walk begins at the designated car park in Blairmore. Availability is not guaranteed, and hikers should arrive with a backup plan if the area is full.

intel.title: Local Supplies
intel.text: Evidence does not specify fuel or supply points in Blairmore; verify availability in larger nearby settlements like Kinlochbervie before arrival.

intel.title: Connectivity Status
intel.text: Signal strength across the moorland and at the bay is not documented in official sources. Prepare for a total lack of mobile coverage during the hike.

plan.arrival: Drive to the trailhead at Blairmore, ensuring all supplies are gathered beforehand as the area is remote and rural.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is suitable for reaching the Blairmore car park, though roads in the Highlands can be narrow; check for local width restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Am Buachaille sea-stack provides a dramatic silhouette during the late afternoon light, depending on the season.
